findings.F1: The pooled result is near zero because the effect has opposite signs by weekend volume, and the two cancel. On my 1,803 Sunday-close cases, the 48-hour unusual return regressed on the weekend's 48-hour move (in the coin's own move units) gives a slope of 0.00045 (t 0.26). Adding the interaction of the weekend move with the log weekday-to-weekend volume ratio gives a strongly negative interaction (−0.018, t −6.75), so reversal grows with thinness.
findings.F2: The reversal is graded across volume-ratio quintiles. The slope of the next 48 hours on the weekend move is +0.0094 (t 3.06) in the quintile where the weekend was busier than the weekdays (median ratio 0.81). It turns negative in the higher quintiles: −0.0044 (t −1.26), −0.0090 (t −2.12), −0.0064 (t −1.49), and −0.0192 (t −3.40) at a median ratio of 3.22.
findings.F3: Weekends that traded heavier than their weekdays carry the largest moves and these moves continue, which is what drags the test's supporting mean to −0.29 % per case. In the thickest volume tercile (mean absolute weekend move 5.4 %), the move in the reversal direction over the next 48 hours averages −1.07 % (t −3.19, 631 cases). In the thinnest tercile (mean absolute move 2.3 %), it averages +0.50 % (t 2.08, 631 cases).
findings.F4: Inside thin weekends the reversal sits in the largest moves. In the thinnest volume tercile, the 48-hour reversal is +1.36 % for the largest third of weekend moves (t 2.87, 211 cases), against +0.10 % (t 0.30) and +0.05 % (t 0.11) for the small and middle thirds.
findings.F5: The thin-weekend reversal is broad but not uniform across coins and years. In the thinnest tercile the slope is negative for 5 of 6 coins (LTC −0.025, t −2.24; ETH −0.015, t −1.80; BTC −0.0097, t −1.56; ZEC alone +0.009 on 32 cases). It is negative in 7 of 8 years (2024 −0.025, t −2.44; 2022 −0.013, t −2.18; 2023 alone +0.009, t 0.94).
findings.F6: Testing another horizon or the comparison with weekday moves would not have cleared the result. Over all weekends the slope stays flat at every horizon, from 12 to 120 hours (t from −0.64 to 0.92). The preceding five weekdays' move against the next 48 hours gives t −1.60, so plain weekend moves are not reversed more than weekday moves.

ideas.idea: A coin's Saturday-Sunday move is partly reversed over the next 48 hours (Monday and Tuesday), only while its weekend volume is lower than its mean volume over the preceding five weekdays; the larger the weekend move and the lower the weekend volume against the weekdays, the larger the share reversed.
ideas.consequence: After a large weekend move on volume below the week's, a trader leans against the move into Tuesday, and refuses that trade when the weekend traded as heavily as the week.
ideas.name: thin weekend large moves reverse

ideas.idea: A coin's Saturday-Sunday move made on higher volume than its mean over the preceding five weekdays continues in the same direction over the next 48 hours, the more so the larger the move and the heavier the weekend volume against the weekdays.
ideas.consequence: A weekend move on heavy volume is a reason to follow it into Monday and Tuesday, not to fade it.
ideas.name: heavy weekend moves continue
